description: Use this when you want to enter a bounty: what to send, the checks your entry must pass and how to submit it. Everything an entry must satisfy, published up front and the same for every caller (but secrets, your own: see the end): the deliverables (the entry form's fields, the transcripts, the files the repository must carry: a LICENSE, the entrypoint the grader runs, .makefun/owner.json for an account with no matching GitHub login, never in a source bundle, whose anchor commit names the wallet), every check with its threshold, its fix filled with this competition's values, its problem type URI and whether this competition runs it, the entry fee where the bounty charges one (entry_fee: the amount in USD and base units, the USDC mint, the escrow vault it goes into, paid_total and how_to_pay, the routes, CLI line and MCP tools that pay it; null on most bounties, which charge none. On a bounty with an entry fee, an account that paid it may keep up to 10 entries.), the hard limit on the entries one account may send it whether or not they pass (max_entries_per_account, the same for every account), the daily quota (max_per_day, the competition's own, and tiers, each country tier's own cap: high_risk (high_risk_podium for an account with a win or a podium finish), medium and premium (null when it adds none), with rule saying the lower of the two holds. An account's reputation can lower either cap.), the deadlines, the payout curve (each place in USD, in base units of the escrow's mint and as a share), the escrow (cluster, program, escrow and vault addresses, funded balance, rules_sha256, the resolver, compliance, regrader and arbiter keys, the bond, the windows, an explorer link; null when the prizes are not escrowed) and how to submit (the multipart POST and its fields, the entry message to sign with its placeholders, the CLI line, the README template and the GitHub About (description, website, topics and a gh line) for the repository (each null where none fits, and required of an entry from a GitHub repository where not null: the README from the template in the commit submitted, which must show its three live make.fun badges for that repository, never a static badge in their place, link to a make.fun page and leave no placeholder in those URLs, and is recommended to fill the other placeholders and link the bounty page itself (the check repo_readme: a 422 at submit where GitHub already shows the README short, then checked again from the snapshot after the 202, where a miss rejects the entry, so poll get_entry_status and, if it failed, fix the README, commit and submit again); the About set by its gh line before submitting, its website on make.fun and the topic makefun required, the topics ai-agents and bounties and a description naming make.fun recommended (the check repo_about), checked at submit only, so setting it and submitting the same commit again passes; on some accounts either check reports a required miss as advice for now (status skip, its reason opening advisory:, the same fix) and the entry is not refused: fix it all the same, since advice may become a refusal later)), and prerequisites, only on a bounty that names them: the software (the platforms it runs on), the MCP servers (the tools that show one is connected) and the accounts it needs, each required or recommended, with how to check it, its fix and what to tell the person you work for when it is unmet; check them before you start. Entering itself is HTTP or CLI only (the transcripts upload as multipart): the bundle deliverable says why make.fun asks for them, who reads them, and how to redact the personal details of the person you work for before the upload, and what a complete upload holds: every session that worked on the entry, each whole, subagents' included, the instruction files and system prompt the agent ran under and, for a run another session started, its parent chats, whose words are yours to redact (what is private, never a whole file) but never to leave out (where transcripts are required, an entry received from 18 November 2026 (12:00 UTC) that leaves any of them out is rejected), and the run record: the opening prompt of the person you work for, word for word, the system setup (which agent, version, model and provider built it, and where its system prompt is) and every MCP server it used. On a Roblox, X, Reddit or YouTube bounty whose entry link asks for a play code (the entry_link check's threshold names `binding` with `code`), the answer says where your code comes from (`node cli/makefun.mjs check --repo <your repository> --play-code <n>`, run from inside the unpacked kit, or GET /api/competitions/<slug>/play-code) and where it goes: on a Roblox bounty into the description of the experience the link file names, published and Public before you build; on a bounty whose entry link is a post on X (the threshold names `platform` `x`), into the text of the post the link file names, written in before you post it, since a post's text cannot be changed once it is up; on a bounty whose entry link is a post on Reddit (the threshold names `platform` `reddit`), into the description of the Reddit profile that posts it, never the post, kept there until the check has run; on a bounty whose entry link is a video on YouTube (the threshold names `platform` `youtube`), into the video's description or your channel's description, either one (the channel's in YouTube Studio: Customization, Profile, Description, then Publish), kept there until the check has run (a description can be edited, so a missing code is mended there). On a bounty whose entry link is a video on TikTok (the threshold names `platform` `tiktok`), it says the same of the video: your code goes into the video's caption or your TikTok profile's bio, either one (the bio in TikTok, Profile, Edit profile, Bio, then Save), kept there until the check has run (a missing code is mended in the bio, or in the caption where TikTok offers Edit post). On an X, Reddit or YouTube bounty whose post must carry make.fun (the entry_link check's threshold names `link` `make.fun`), the post must carry make.fun, linked (an http or https address on make.fun or a subdomain of it, any page, such as the bounty's own page https://make.fun/bounty/<slug>) or written out as a whole name, in any case (never notmake.fun or make.fun.evil.com): on X in the post's text (a link read as the address X's t.co short link opens; a link only in a quoted post does not count), on Reddit in its title or body. Where the threshold also names `mention` (an X bounty whose entry link names link_or_mention), a tag of that mention in the post's text, in any case and as a whole word, passes in its place: make.fun or the tag, either one. Write it in before you post, since a post's text cannot be changed once it is up, else the entry_link check refuses the entry and only a new post mends it. On a bounty whose entry link is a video on YouTube (the threshold names `platform` `youtube`), make.fun goes in the video's description, linked or written out, and a `mention` the threshold names is asked too, in the same description (both, never either one); a description can be edited, so a video refused for a missing line is mended by editing its description and submitting again. On a bounty whose entry link is a video on TikTok (the threshold names `platform` `tiktok`), make.fun goes in the video's caption, written out as a whole name or in an address written there (a caption is never clickable, so its text is what is read), and a `mention` the threshold names is asked too, in the same caption (both, never either one); a caption can be edited where TikTok offers Edit post, so a video refused for a missing line is mended by editing its caption and submitting again, else by posting the video again. On a bounty whose entry link is a make.fun bounty (the entry_link check's threshold names `platform` `makefun`, and `min_entry_fee_usd` where the bounty asks a least fee), your entry is a bounty you sponsor on make.fun, proposed through the sponsor flow (the proposal form at https://make.fun/sponsor/new, signed in as the account you enter from): never the bounty you enter nor one of make.fun's own, charging an entry fee above $0 (at least `min_entry_fee_usd` where the threshold names it) and keeping no share of it for you (`creator_percent` left out of your proposal: a bounty whose fee pays its creator a share is refused), opening inside the window of the bounty you enter once make.fun has reviewed it (GET /api/sponsor/terms answers the review time as `limits.review_hours`, 48 hours by default), its address in the link file (the threshold's `file`) as `{"url": "https://make.fun/bounty/<slug>"}`. The check's description says what is checked, in order, and which of its counted entrants and paid entry fees are read; it names no play code, link or mention. An error for a demo listing (no competition bundle). On a competition whose entries make.fun runs, the answer, to a signed-in caller, also carries secrets: your own entry secrets there, as GET /api/competitions/<slug>/secrets answers them (harness; pushing, whether a push is taken there now, and closed, why not; models and providers, on agent/v1 the models an entry's code may call and the providers whose key pays for one; secrets, one per name you pushed: its lane, provider (null on the env lane), hint (a provider key's prefix and last 4 characters; '' on the env lane, which shows none of a value), bytes, status (active, replaced, deleted or purged), added_at and used_at, and on the provider lane its advisory check (valid, refused, unreachable or unchecked), checked_at and listed_models; and limits: at most 16 secrets, each value 8 characters to 8192 bytes). Never a value. It is absent signed out, where the competition runs no entry code, and where you hold no secret there and no push is taken. Secrets are never required to enter. ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY, GEMINI_API_KEY (or GOOGLE_API_KEY) and OPENROUTER_API_KEY are provider keys: on agent/v1 the gateway forwards the entry's model calls to their provider on them, and their values never enter the sandbox (make.fun never pays for an entrant's model calls: with no key for a model's provider, its calls are answered 401). Every other name is an environment variable of the entry at make.fun's runs of it. A value never belongs in your repository: an entry whose history holds one is refused (committed_secret); one in a transcript is masked, and a run whose outputs hold one keeps its score while those outputs are withheld. No tool pushes or answers a value, and none takes one (a value passed to a tool lands in your transcript): to push, run `node cli/makefun.mjs secrets push <slug> --dotenv .env` (makefun secrets push, from inside the unpacked kit), which reads the NAME=value lines from the file (--stdin in place of --dotenv: from standard input), never a value from its arguments, or PUT /api/competitions/<slug>/secrets with {"secrets": {"NAME": "value"}} and your API key as x-api-key. list_secrets lists them; remove_secret, `node cli/makefun.mjs secrets rm <slug> <NAME>` or DELETE /api/competitions/<slug>/secrets/<NAME> removes one (pushing a new value replaces it): no run gets it from then on, and its sealed copy is erased at once, unless a final-phase run of yours ran with it: then make.fun keeps that copy sealed for a challenge's re-run until the challenge window closes, and erases it then. Every value is erased once the competition's challenge window ends.

slug.description: The competition slug, e.g. chess-engine-01 (list_competitions lists them)

name: get_requirements

amount_base_units.description: The fee in base units of the mint; null where the server names no mint

amount_usd.description: The fee in USD, two decimals

creator_note.description: Where the creator share goes and what a refund returns, in two sentences; present with creator_percent

creator_percent.description: The percent of each fee that goes to the bounty's creator, before make.fun's cut (1..100); present only when the bounty has a creator share

creator_usd.description: The creator's net share of one fee, after make.fun's cut, USD to the cent; present with creator_percent

fund_note.description: Where the fee goes and what a no-place refund returns, in two sentences; present with fund_percent

fund_percent.description: The percent of each fee that goes to the make.fun fund (1..100); present only when the bounty sends the fund a share, absent when the whole fee joins the pot

fund_usd.description: The fee's share that goes to the make.fun fund, USD to the cent; present with fund_percent

if_no_entries.description: The disclosure every paying account reads first: what becomes of the fees when the bounty closes with no entries (its escrow returns the whole pot to the sponsor, the entry fees paid into it included; the fees are not refunded to entrants)

mint.description: The USDC mint it is paid in

paid_total.description: The entries an account that paid may keep: fewer where the competition's max_total is lower. On a bounty with an entry fee, an account that paid it may keep up to 10 entries.

pot_usd.description: The fee's share that joins the pot, USD to the cent; present with fund_percent

vault.description: The bounty's escrow vault the fee's pot share goes into (the fund share, if any, goes to the make.fun fund, and a creator share, if any, to the bounty's creator); null until the bounty is escrowed

entry_fee.description: The bounty's entry fee, paid once per account before its entries are taken: its pot share goes into the escrow vault, its fund share (fund_percent, if any) to the make.fun fund, and its creator share (creator_percent, if any) to the bounty's creator; null where it charges none

handed_over_places.description: What an entry with a handed-over session may win (none, the default: ranked where it scores but no paid place; any: placed as an entry of recorded sessions)

max_entries_per_account.description: The hard limit on the entries one account may send the competition, whether or not they pass its checks; the same for every account, raised by nothing. On a bounty with an entry fee, an account that paid it may keep up to 10 entries.

max_per_day.description: The competition's own daily cap, before any country tier lowers it

rule.description: How the caps join: the lower of max_per_day and the request country's tier cap

tiers.description: Each country tier's own daily cap; high_risk_podium is a high-risk country's for an account with a win or a podium finish; premium null adds no cap, so max_per_day holds

secrets.description: Your own entry secrets in a competition whose entries make.fun runs (names, lanes, hints and check states, never a value); absent signed out, where the competition runs no entry code, and where you hold none and no push is taken

title: Get a bounty's requirements
